jazariyya.title: المقدمة فيما على قارئ القرآن أن يعلمه (الجزرية)

jazariyya.editor: د. عبد المحسن بن محمد القاسم (ط 2، 1441هـ/2020م)

notes.gloss: gloss is a one-line English summary of what the line teaches, written for this app. It is not a translation.
notes.text: sadr/ajuz are the edition text exactly as on the Shamela page (Unicode code points kept as published), with footnote markers removed. Compare text after Unicode NFC normalisation; the Jazariyya page stores shadda before the vowel.
notes.verified: two-copies = compared word by word by script against a second copy (see docs/05-mutun-verification.md). It is not the two-person check against the printed book that spec C7 requires.
notes.section: section is an app label from the edition's headings, not part of the matn.
notes.rules: An empty rules list means the line teaches a topic with no app rule id yet (Tuhfa 29: لام الفعل).

lines.gloss: The author names himself: Sulayman al-Jamzuri, hoping for the mercy of the Forgiving.
Opens with praise of Allah and blessings on the Prophet, his family and those who follow.
States the topic: a poem for the learner on noon sakinah, tanween and the madd.
Names the poem Tuhfat al-Atfal and credits his teacher al-Mihi.

variants.source: Quranpedia book 18289 (الشرح المبسط المفيد لما تضمنه نظم الجمزورية); Quranpedia 21539 (تحفة الأطفال، ت ابن سالم، 2006)

lines.gloss: Hopes it benefits students and earns reward and acceptance.
Noon sakinah and tanween have four rulings.
First ruling: izhar (clear noon) before the six throat letters.
Lists the six throat letters: hamza, ha, ayn, ha, ghayn, kha.
Second ruling: idgham (merging) into the six letters of يرملون.

variants.source: Quranpedia 21539 (تحفة الأطفال، ت ابن سالم، 2006)

lines.gloss: Idgham with ghunnah happens in the four letters of ينمو.
Exception: no merging when noon and the letter are in one word, as in دنيا and صنوان.
Idgham without ghunnah happens in lam and ra.

variants.source: Quranpedia 21539 (تحفة الأطفال، ت ابن سالم، 2006)

lines.gloss: Third ruling: iqlab, turning noon into meem with ghunnah before ba, with ikhfa.
Fourth ruling: ikhfa (hiding) before the remaining letters is required.

lines.sadr: فِي خَمْسَةٍ مِنْ بَعْدِ عَشْرٍ رَمْزُهَا
lines.ajuz: فِي كِلْمِ هَذَا البَيْتِ قَد ضَّمَّنْتُهَا
lines.gloss: The ikhfa letters are fifteen, coded in the first letters of the next line.

lines.sadr: صِفْ ذَا ثَنَا كَمْ جَادَ شَخْصٌ قَدْ سَمَا
lines.ajuz: دُمْ طَيِّبًا زِدْ فِي تُقًى ضَعْ ظَالِمَا
lines.gloss: The code line whose word initials give the fifteen ikhfa letters.
Make ghunnah on doubled meem and noon; each is called a letter of ghunnah.

lines.sadr: وَالمِيمُ إِنْ تَسْكُنْ تَجِي قَبْلَ الْهِجَا
lines.gloss: Meem sakinah comes before any letter except the soft alif.

variants.source: Quranpedia book 18289 (الشرح المبسط المفيد لما تضمنه نظم الجمزورية)

lines.gloss: Meem sakinah has three rulings: ikhfa, idgham and izhar.
First: ikhfa before ba, called the labial (shafawi) ikhfa.
Second: idgham into another meem, called the small idgham.

variants.source: Quranpedia book 18289 (الشرح المبسط المفيد لما تضمنه نظم الجمزورية)
Quranpedia 21539 (تحفة الأطفال، ت ابن سالم، 2006)

lines.gloss: Third: izhar before all other letters, called labial izhar.

variants.source: Quranpedia book 18289 (الشرح المبسط المفيد لما تضمنه نظم الجمزورية)

lines.sadr: وَاحْذَرْ لَدَى وَاوٍ وَفَا أَنْ تَخْتَفِي
lines.gloss: Take care to keep meem clear before waw and fa, because of nearness and shared place.
The lam of al- has two states; the first is izhar.

lines.sadr: قَبْلَ ارْبَعٍ مَعْ عَشْرَةٍ خُذْ عِلْمَهُ
lines.gloss: Izhar before fourteen letters, gathered in ابغ حجك وخف عقيمه.
The second state: idgham into the other fourteen letters, coded in the next line.

lines.sadr: طِبْ ثُمَّ صِلْ رُحْمًا تَفُزْ ضِفْ ذَا نِعَمْ
lines.ajuz: دَعْ سُوءَ ظَنٍّ زُرْ شَرِيفًا لِلْكَرَمْ
lines.gloss: The code line whose word initials give the fourteen sun letters.
Call the first lam qamariyyah (moon) and the second shamsiyyah (sun).

lines.ajuz: فِي نَحْوِ قُلْ نَعَمْ وَقُلْنَا وَالْتَقَى
lines.gloss: The lam of a verb is always pronounced clearly, as in قل نعم، قلنا، التقى.

variants.source: Quranpedia book 18289 (الشرح المبسط المفيد لما تضمنه نظم الجمزورية)

lines.gloss: Two letters sharing makhraj and qualities are called mithlan (identical).
Letters close in makhraj and different in qualities are called mutaqaribayn.
Letters sharing a makhraj but not qualities are called mutajanisayn.
If the first of the two letters has sukun, the pair is called saghir (small).

lines.sadr: أَوْ حُرِّكَ الحَرْفَانِ فِي كُلٍّ فَقُلْ
lines.gloss: If both letters are voweled, the pair is called kabir (big).
Madd is original (asli) or secondary (far'i); the original is called natural (tabi'i).

variants.source: Quranpedia book 18289 (الشرح المبسط المفيد لما تضمنه نظم الجمزورية)

lines.sadr: مَا لاَ تَوَقُّفٌ لَهُ عَلَى سَبَبْ
lines.gloss: Natural madd needs no cause, and the letter cannot be said without it.

lines.sadr: بلْ أَيُّ حَرْفٍ غَيْرُ هَمْزٍ أَوْ سُكُونْ
lines.gloss: Any madd letter not followed by hamza or sukun is natural madd.
Secondary madd depends on a cause: a hamza or a sukun.
The three madd letters are in the word واي, as found in نوحيها.

lines.sadr: وَالكَسْرُ قَبْلَ الْيَا وَقَبْلَ الْواوِ ضَمْ
lines.gloss: Conditions: kasra before ya, damma before waw, fatha before alif.
The soft (lin) letters are ya and waw with sukun after a fatha.
Madd has three rulings: obligatory, permitted and necessary.

lines.sadr: فَوَاجِبٌ إِنْ جَاءَ هَمْزٌ بَعْدَ مَدْ
lines.gloss: Obligatory: hamza after a madd letter in the same word; called muttasil (joined).
Permitted: madd and hamza in separate words, lengthened or shortened; called munfasil.
Also permitted: a sukun that appears only on stopping, as in تعلمون، نستعين.

lines.sadr: أَوْ قُدِّمَ الْهَمْزُ عَلَى المَدِّ وَذَا
lines.gloss: Also permitted: hamza before the madd letter, called badal, as in آمنوا، إيمانا.
Necessary (lazim): a fixed sukun after the madd letter in joining and stopping; lengthen it.
Lazim madd has four kinds: word (kalimi) and letter (harfi).

variants.source: Quranpedia book 18289 (الشرح المبسط المفيد لما تضمنه نظم الجمزورية)

lines.gloss: Each is either light (mukhaffaf) or heavy (muthaqqal), making four.

lines.ajuz: مَعْ حَرْفِ مَدٍّ فَهْوَ كِلْمِيٌّ وَقَعْ
lines.gloss: Kalimi: the sukun meets a madd letter inside a word.
Harfi: in a three-letter letter-name whose middle letter is a madd letter.
Heavy if the sukun is merged (idgham), light if it is not.
Harfi lazim occurs at the openings of surahs, in eight letters.
The eight letters of كم عسل نقص; ayn has two ways, the long one preferred.

lines.sadr: وَمَا سِوَى الحَرْفِ الثُّلاَثِي لاَ أَلِفْ
lines.gloss: Letter-names other than three-letter ones (and not alif) get natural madd.

variants.source: Quranpedia book 18289 (الشرح المبسط المفيد لما تضمنه نظم الجمزورية)

lines.gloss: These two-letter openings are the letters of حي طاهر.
All fourteen opening letters are gathered in صله سحيرا من قطعك.
The poem is complete, with endless praise to Allah.
Gives the line count and the date of composition in abjad numbers.

variants.source: Quranpedia 21539 (تحفة الأطفال، ت ابن سالم، 2006)
Quranpedia 21539 (تحفة الأطفال، ت ابن سالم، 2006)

lines.gloss: Ends with blessings and peace on the Prophet Ahmad, seal of the prophets.
And on his family, companions, followers, every reciter and every listener.
The author names himself: Muhammad Ibn al-Jazari al-Shafi'i, hoping for his Lord's pardon.

variants.source: Shamela 12093 (المقدمة الجزرية، ط المغني 1422/2001); not in al-Qasim's footnotes

lines.gloss: Praise of Allah and blessings on His chosen Prophet.
Blessings on Muhammad, his family, companions, the Quran teacher and those who love him.
This is an introduction to what the reciter must know.
It is a duty for reciters to learn these things before they start.
They must know the makharij and sifat to speak in the most eloquent way.
They must master tajweed, the stops, and how words are written in the mushaf.

lines.ajuz: وَتَاءِ أُنْثَى لَمْ تَكُنْ تُكْتَبْ بِـ «هَا»
lines.gloss: Including cut and joined words, and the feminine ta not written as ha.

variants.source: Shamela 12093 (المقدمة الجزرية، ط المغني 1422/2001); not in al-Qasim's footnotes

lines.gloss: There are seventeen makharij, on the view chosen by the experts.
Alif and its two sisters (madd letters) come from the jawf and end with the air.
Deepest throat: hamza and ha; middle throat: ayn and ha.
Nearest throat: ghayn and kha; qaf from the back of the tongue, then kaf.
Kaf lower; jeem, sheen, ya from the middle; dad from the tongue's side.
Dad touches the molars, left or right; lam from the edge to the tip.
Noon from the tip, below lam; ra near it, closer to the back of the tongue.
Ta, dal, ta from the tip with the upper incisors; the whistling letters rest...
...from the tip above the lower incisors; tha, dhal, tha toward the upper ones.
From the two tips; fa from inside the lower lip with the edges of the upper incisors.
Waw, ba, meem from the two lips; ghunnah comes from the nose.
Qualities: jahr, rikhwah, istifal, infitah, ismat, and their opposites.
Hams letters: فحثه شخص سكت; shiddah letters: أجد قط بكت.
Between soft and strong: لن عمر; the seven high letters: خص ضغط قظ.
Itbaq: sad, dad, ta, za; idhlaq letters: فر من لب.
Safir: sad, zay, seen; qalqalah: قطب جد; and lin...
...is waw and ya with sukun after a fatha; inhiraf is true of...
...lam and ra; ra has takrir; sheen has tafashshi; dad has istitalah.
Applying tajweed is a firm duty; whoever does not correct his Quran is sinful.

variants.source: Shamela 12093 (المقدمة الجزرية، ط المغني 1422/2001); also recorded in al-Qasim's footnotes

lines.gloss: Because Allah revealed it with tajweed, and so it reached us.
Tajweed is also the ornament of recitation and the beauty of performance.
Definition: giving each letter its right of qualities, inherent and resulting...
...returning each letter to its makhraj, and saying it the same way wherever it occurs...
...complete, without strain, gently, without excess.
Between knowing it and leaving it there is only practice with the jaw.
Make low letters light, and avoid making alif heavy.
Keep light the hamza of الحمد، أعوذ، اهدنا، الله and the lam of لله، لنا...
...وليتلطف، وعلى الله، ولا الضالين, and meem in مخمصة and مرض.
Keep ba light in برق، باطل، بهم، بذي; keep its shiddah and jahr...

variants.source: Shamela 12093 (المقدمة الجزرية، ط المغني 1422/2001); also recorded in al-Qasim's footnotes

lines.gloss: ...in ba and jeem, as in حب، الصبر، ربوة، اجتثت، حج، الفجر.

lines.ajuz: وَإِنْ يَكُنْ فِي الوَقْفِ كَانَ أَبْيَنَا
lines.gloss: Make qalqalah clear on a sakin qalqalah letter, clearer when stopping.
Make ha clear in حصحص، أحطت، الحق and seen in مستقيم، يسطو، يسقو.

variants.source: Shamela 12093 (المقدمة الجزرية، ط المغني 1422/2001); not in al-Qasim's footnotes

lines.gloss: Make ra light when it has kasra, or has sukun after a kasra...

lines.sadr: إِنْ لَمْ تَكُنْ مِنْ قَبْلِ حَرْفِ اسْتِعْلَا
lines.gloss: ...unless a high letter follows it, or the kasra before it is not original.
Both ways are allowed in فرق; and hide the takrir of a doubled ra.

lines.ajuz: عَنْ فَتْحٍ اَوْ ضَمٍّ كَـ «عَبْدُ اللَّهِ»
lines.gloss: Make the lam of Allah heavy after a fatha or damma, as in عبد الله.
Make the high letters heavy, the itbaq letters most of all, as in قال and العصا.

variants.source: Shamela 12093 (المقدمة الجزرية، ط المغني 1422/2001); also recorded in al-Qasim's footnotes

lines.gloss: Keep itbaq in أحطت and بسطت; نخلقكم has two ways.
Keep the sukun clear in جعلنا، أنعمت، المغضوب، ضللنا.
Keep the open sound in محذورا، عسى so they are not confused with محظورا، عصى.
Keep the shiddah in kaf and ta, as in شرككم، تتوفى، فتنة.

lines.ajuz: أَدْغِمْ؛ كَـ «قُلْ رَبِّ» وَ «بَلْ لَا»، وَأَبِنْ
lines.gloss: Merge a sakin first letter into an identical or same-kind letter, as in قل رب، بل لا...

variants.source: Shamela 12093 (المقدمة الجزرية، ط المغني 1422/2001); not in al-Qasim's footnotes

lines.gloss: ...but keep clear in في يوم، قالوا وهم، قل نعم، سبحه، لا تزغ قلوب، فالتقم.
Tell dad from za by istitalah and makhraj; all za words come in...
The list of za words begins: الظعن، ظل، الظهر، عظم، الحفظ، أيقظ...
The za word list continues: ظاهر، لظى، شواظ، كظم، ظلما...

variants.source: Shamela 12093 (المقدمة الجزرية، ط المغني 1422/2001); not in al-Qasim's footnotes

lines.sadr: أَظْفَرَ، ظَنّاً كَيْفَ جَا، وَعِظْ» سِوَى
lines.gloss: Continues, except عضين; ظل in al-Nahl and al-Zukhruf.
Continues: ظلت، ظلتم، ظلوا in al-Rum, ظلت in al-Hijr, نظل in al-Shu'ara.

variants.source: Shamela 12093 (المقدمة الجزرية، ط المغني 1422/2001); also recorded in al-Qasim's footnotes

lines.gloss: Continues: يظللن، محظورا، المحتظر، فظا, and every النظر...
...except in ويل and هل and the first ناضرة; الغيظ except in al-Ra'd and Hud.

variants.source: Shamela 12093 (المقدمة الجزرية، ط المغني 1422/2001); not in al-Qasim's footnotes

lines.gloss: الحظ but not الحض على الطعام; ظنين has a known difference of reading.

variants.source: Shamela 12093 (المقدمة الجزرية، ط المغني 1422/2001); also recorded in al-Qasim's footnotes

lines.gloss: When dad and za meet, keep them clear: أنقض ظهرك، يعض الظالم.
Keep clear اضطر، وعظت، أفضتم, and keep ha pure in جباههم، عليهم.
Show the ghunnah of doubled noon and meem, and hide...

lines.ajuz: بَاءٍ عَلَى المُخْتَارِ مِنْ أَهْلِ الأَدَا
lines.gloss: ...a sakin meem with ghunnah before ba, the chosen view of the experts.

variants.source: Shamela 12093 (المقدمة الجزرية، ط المغني 1422/2001); not in al-Qasim's footnotes
Shamela 12093 (المقدمة الجزرية، ط المغني 1422/2001); not in al-Qasim's footnotes

lines.ajuz: وَاحْذَرْ لَدَى وَاوٍ وَفَا: أَنْ تَخْتَفِي
lines.gloss: Keep meem clear before other letters; take care before waw and fa.
Tanween and noon sakinah: izhar, idgham, iqlab, ikhfa.

variants.source: Shamela 12093 (المقدمة الجزرية، ط المغني 1422/2001); not in al-Qasim's footnotes

lines.ajuz: فِي اللَّامِ وَالرَّا لَا بِغُنَّةٍ لَزِمْ
lines.gloss: Izhar before throat letters; idgham without ghunnah in lam and ra, always.
Idgham with ghunnah in the letters of يومن, except inside one word: دنيا، عنونوا.
Iqlab before ba with ghunnah; ikhfa before the other letters.

variants.source: Shamela 12093 (المقدمة الجزرية، ط المغني 1422/2001); not in al-Qasim's footnotes

lines.gloss: Madd is necessary, obligatory or permitted; permitted allows long or short.

lines.sadr: فَلَازِمٌ: إِنْ جَاءَ بَعْدَ حَرْفِ مَدْ
lines.gloss: Necessary: a sukun fixed in both states after a madd letter; lengthen it fully.
Obligatory: madd before a hamza joined in the same word.
Permitted: madd separated from the hamza, or a sukun made by stopping.
After the letters, you must know where to stop...
...and where to start; stops are of three kinds: tamm, kafi, hasan.

variants.source: Shamela 12093 (المقدمة الجزرية، ط المغني 1422/2001); also recorded in al-Qasim's footnotes

lines.sadr: وَهْيَ لِمَا تَمَّ؛ فَإِنْ لَمْ يُوجَدِ
lines.gloss: They come where the meaning is complete; with no link to what follows, or only a meaning link, start after it.
Tamm, then kafi; with a link in wording do not restart, except at verse ends; that is hasan.
Stopping where the meaning is incomplete is qabih; if forced, stop and restart from before.

variants.source: Shamela 12093 (المقدمة الجزرية، ط المغني 1422/2001); also recorded in al-Qasim's footnotes

lines.sadr: وَلَيْسَ فِي القُرْآنِ مِنْ وَقْفٍ وَجَبْ
lines.ajuz: وَلَا حَرَامٌ؛ غَيْرُ مَا لَهُ سَبَبْ
lines.gloss: No stop in the Quran is obligatory and none forbidden, except for a reason.

lines.ajuz: فِي المُصْحَفِ الإِمَامِ فِيمَا قَدْ أَتَى
lines.gloss: Learn the cut and joined words, and the ta, as written in the Imam mushaf.

variants.source: Shamela 12093 (المقدمة الجزرية، ط المغني 1422/2001); also recorded in al-Qasim's footnotes

lines.gloss: Write أن لا cut in ten places, with ملجأ and لا إله إلا...

variants.source: Shamela 12093 (المقدمة الجزرية، ط المغني 1422/2001); also recorded in al-Qasim's footnotes

lines.gloss: ...تعبدوا in Ya-Sin, the second in Hud, يشركن، تشرك، يدخلن، تعلوا على...

lines.sadr: أَنْ لَا يَقُولُوا، لَا أَقُولَ»، «إِنْ مَا»
lines.gloss: ...أن لا يقولوا، لا أقول; إن ما in al-Ra'd cut, the open one joined; عن ما...

variants.source: Shamela 12093 (المقدمة الجزرية، ط المغني 1422/2001); not in al-Qasim's footnotes
Shamela 12093 (المقدمة الجزرية، ط المغني 1422/2001); not in al-Qasim's footnotes

lines.gloss: ...نهوا cut; من ما in al-Rum and al-Nisa, differing in al-Munafiqun; أم من أسس...
...in Fussilat, al-Nisa, al-Saffat; حيث ما; أن لم with fatha; إن ما with kasra...
...in al-An'am; the open أن ما يدعون in two places; differing in al-Anfal and al-Nahl.

variants.source: Shamela 12093 (المقدمة الجزرية، ط المغني 1422/2001); not in al-Qasim's footnotes

lines.gloss: كل ما سألتموه cut; differing in ردوا and قل بئسما; describe joining...
...in خلفتموني and اشتروا; cut في ما in أوحي، أفضتم، اشتهت، يبلو...

variants.source: Shamela 12093 (المقدمة الجزرية، ط المغني 1422/2001); also recorded in al-Qasim's footnotes

lines.gloss: ...the second in fa'alna, al-Waqi'ah, al-Rum, the two Tanzil, al-Zulla; join elsewhere.

variants.source: Shamela 12093 (المقدمة الجزرية، ط المغني 1422/2001); also recorded in al-Qasim's footnotes

lines.gloss: Join فأينما as in al-Nahl; it differs in al-Shu'ara, al-Ahzab, al-Nisa.
Join فإلم in Hud, ألن نجعل، نجمع، كيلا تحزنوا، تأسوا على...
...الحج، عليك حرج; they cut عن من يشاء، من تولى، يوم هم...
...مال هذا، الذين، هؤلاء; تحين is joined in the Imam mushaf, though that is questioned.

variants.source: Shamela 12093 (المقدمة الجزرية، ط المغني 1422/2001); not in al-Qasim's footnotes

lines.ajuz: كَذَا مِنَ «الْ» وَ «هَا» وَ «يَا»؛ لَا تَفْصِلِ
lines.gloss: Join وزنوهم، كالوهم, and the al-, ha and ya prefixes; do not separate them.

variants.source: Shamela 12093 (المقدمة الجزرية، ط المغني 1422/2001); not in al-Qasim's footnotes
Shamela 12093 (المقدمة الجزرية، ط المغني 1422/2001); also recorded in al-Qasim's footnotes

امرأت in Yusuf, Al Imran, al-Qasas, al-Tahrim; معصيت only in Qad Sami'a.
شجرت in al-Dukhan; سنت in all of Fatir, al-Anfal, and the last in Ghafir.
